children: Science Applications International is becoming a government darling.

SAIC, which provides technology and engineering services to U.S. government agencies, posted better-than-expected earnings and raised its fiscal-year outlook on Monday. The report shows that its federal contract winning streak could continue to boost its earnings momentum.

Management attributed the latest quarter's increased revenue to a higher volume of client contracts, which totaled $1.2 billion during the period, as well as the recent acquisition of software provider SilverEdge Government Solutions.

The company now projects revenue in the range of $7.2 billion to $7.3 billion for the fiscal year ending in January 2027. That's up slightly from a previous range of $7 billion to $7.2 billion and above analysts' forecast for $7.19 billion, according to a FactSet survey.

SAIC also raised its fiscal-year adjusted earnings forecast to between $10.65 and $10.75 a share, compared with its previous outlook of $9.90 to $10.10 a share and Wall Street's estimate of $10.18 a share.
Shares jumped 3.5% to $130.30 on Monday, while the benchmark S&P 500 was down 0.6%.

In the fiscal second quarter ended in July, SAIC posted adjusted earnings of $3.01 a share, beating forecasts for $2.31. Revenue increased 6% from the year-ago period to $1.88 billion, surpassing analysts' calls for $1.76 billion.
The beat-and-raise report continues the momentum from the fiscal first quarter, when the company's solid numbers surprised analysts.

Just earlier this month, SAIC said it won a $400 million recompete contract to design and manage ground-based computer networks and data systems for an undisclosed U.S. intelligence agency. That win brought the company's award value for its Intel Space business to more than $1.6 billion in the first half of fiscal 2027, SAIC said on Aug. 5.
SAIC also secured a $740 million recompete contract in early August with the U.S. Department of Homeland Security to help assess security risk with travelers and cargo entering the country.
SAIC said Monday it will continue to invest in artificial intelligence and quantum to help streamline operations with defense, intelligence, and civilian clients.
SAIC's raised guidance coupled with a strong portfolio could continue to boost investor confidence. The stock has climbed 30% so far this year.
